risk_if_not_implemented: Without Control Assurance Automation (CAA) Oversight, automated control assurance results may be manipulated, misattributed or lose integrity, causing misplaced confidence in control effectiveness. Based on the risk and threat mapping for this control, this deficiency most likely exposes the organization to Unperformed / Unowned Control Responsibilities (R-GV-3), Lack of oversight of internal controls (R-GV-6), Inability to Demonstrate Due Diligence / Due Care (R-GV-9), Unreliable Assurance / Decision Information (R-GV-10), and most likely increases susceptibility to Dysfunctional Management Practices (MT-8), Human Error (MT-9), Statutory / Regulatory / Contractual Change (MT-11), Conflict of Interest (COI) / Undue Influence / Insider Misconduct (MT-15).

compensating_control_1.name: Continuous Control Monitoring (CCM)
compensating_control_1.description: Automated mechanisms exist to perform Continuous Control Monitoring (CCM) to assess and report the conformity status of the organization's Technology Assets, Applications, Services and Data (TAASD) against applicable security, compliance and resilience controls.
compensating_control_1.justification: Continuous Control Monitoring (CCM) (CPL-18) provides detective monitoring capability that compensates for the absence of Control Assurance Automation (CAA) Oversight (CPL-29) by identifying unauthorized, anomalous or non-compliant activity that the primary control would have prevented. Given the process-oriented nature of this control, this compensating control targets the same underlying risk objective through an alternative approach, helping to maintain an acceptable level of residual risk until the primary control can be implemented.

compensating_control_2.name: Conformity Monitoring
compensating_control_2.description: Mechanisms exist to validate that Technology Assets, Applications, Services and/or Data (TAASD) conform to the organization's security, compliance and/or resilience policies, standards and other applicable requirements.
compensating_control_2.justification: Conformity Monitoring (CPL-05) provides detective monitoring capability that compensates for the absence of Control Assurance Automation (CAA) Oversight (CPL-29) by identifying unauthorized, anomalous or non-compliant activity that the primary control would have prevented. Given the process-oriented nature of this control, this compensating control targets the same underlying risk objective through an alternative approach, helping to maintain an acceptable level of residual risk until the primary control can be implemented.
